subject: Social Habits
title: Looking after things
objectives: Children will care for toys, books and their own belongings.
Children will put things back in the right place.
content: My bag and my things, caring for toys and books, and putting things back.
teachingActivities: Give every child a labelled hook and bag; show how to hold a book gently; use pictures on shelves so children can put things back; praise care not just tidiness; replace broken items without shame.
learnerActivities: Care for toys, books and belongings and put things back in the right place.
assessment: Observe whether each child puts things back and handles a book gently.
expectedOutcomes: Puts a toy back where it belongs.

lessons.title: My bag and my things
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will find and care for their own bag and belongings.
successCriteria: Finds their own bag or hook
Puts their things away with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can tell the truth, help and tidy up.
lessons.starter: Show a bag on a hook and say "This is Ada’s bag. It goes on her hook."
teacherActivities: Show how to hang a bag on its hook.
Help each child find their name and hook.
Show how to put a bottle and lunch box in the bag.
learnerActivities: Child puts things in the bag.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to hang a bag on its hook. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Help each child find their name and hook. Children: Child finds their name.
Step 3. Teacher: Show how to put a bottle and lunch box in the bag. Children: Child puts things in the bag.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "I look after my things." Children: Children repeat the sentence.

practical.title: My hook and my bag
practical.safety: Keep bags low and hooks at child height. Check no small objects are in reach of younger children.

differentiation.support: Find the hook together and hang the bag.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to help a friend find their hook.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Finds their own bag or hook
lessons.conclusion: Look at the hooks and say "Everyone has a place."
lessons.homeConnection: Give your child a place at home for their bag and shoes.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find and care for their own bag and belongings" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: My bag, my bag, on my hook it goes.

lessons.title: Caring for toys and books
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will handle toys and books gently.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can tell the truth, help and tidy up.
resources: A puppet who is rough and then gentle
lessons.starter: Show a puppet throwing a book and say "Oh no. Books are for looking, not throwing."
teacherActivities: Show how to hold and turn the pages gently.
Let children look at a book with a friend.
Show how to place toys down gently.
Say "I am gentle with books and toys."
learnerActivities: Child looks at the book gently.
Child puts a toy down gently.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to hold and turn the pages gently. Children: Children watch and copy.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children look at a book with a friend. Children: Child looks at the book gently.
Step 3. Teacher: Show how to place toys down gently. Children: Child puts a toy down gently.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "I am gentle with books and toys." Children: Children repeat the sentence.

practical.title: Gentle with books
steps: Put it back on the shelf.
practical.safety: Use sturdy board books and supervise closely so books are not chewed. Replace torn items without comment.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to show a friend how to hold a book.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How do we hold a book?

lessons.conclusion: Put the books on the shelf and say thank you.
lessons.homeConnection: Read a book together and let your child turn the pages.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "handle toys and books gently" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Putting things back
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will put toys back where they belong using picture labels.
successCriteria: Matches a toy to its label
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can tell the truth, help and tidy up.
lessons.starter: Show a basket with a picture of cars and say "Cars go here. Every toy has a home."
teacherActivities: Show how to match a toy to its picture label.
Let each child pick a toy and find its basket.
Sing the tidy song while working.
learnerActivities: Child puts the toy in the basket.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to match a toy to its picture label. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child pick a toy and find its basket. Children: Child puts the toy in the basket.
Step 3. Teacher: Sing the tidy song while working. Children: Children tidy and sing.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Every toy is home." Children: Children say home.

practical.title: Toy homes
practical.safety: Keep walkways clear and use large toys only. Supervise the tidy-up.

differentiation.support: Match the toy together and name the label.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to check a basket for the right toys.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Look at the tidy shelves and clap.
lessons.homeConnection: Make picture labels for toy boxes at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "put toys back where they belong using picture labels" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Looking after our classroom
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will share responsibility for the classroom and its things.
successCriteria: Tidies and cares with a friend
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can tell the truth, help and tidy up.
lessons.starter: Say "This is our class. We look after our things together."
teacherActivities: Walk around and notice things to put back.
Give each child a job such as books, blocks or cups.
Give a sticker to every helper.
learnerActivities: Child receives a sticker and says thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Walk around and notice things to put back. Children: Children walk and look.
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child a job such as books, blocks or cups. Children: Child does a job.
Step 3. Teacher: Remind children to be gentle. Children: Child reminds a friend gently.
Step 4. Teacher: Give a sticker to every helper. Children: Child receives a sticker and says thank you.

practical.title: Class care
practical.safety: Supervise closely and use only safe items. Keep stickers away from mouths.

differentiation.support: Work beside the child and name the jobs.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the job allocator.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Cares for the classroom with a friend
lessons.homeConnection: Show your child how to look after the family’s things.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "share responsibility for the classroom and its things" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?

lessons.title: Week 7 caring check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child cares for belongings.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can tell the truth, help and tidy up.
lessons.starter: Sing the caring song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: bags, books and toys.
At each station watch how the child cares.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: bags, books and toys. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child cares. Children: Child cares with a prompt.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Caring stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep walkways clear. Use sturdy items only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to show a friend how to care for a book.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: finds own bag; handles books gently; puts toys back; helps keep the class tidy.

questions.question: How do we hold a book?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 7
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep showing how to care for things at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child cares for belongings" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
